I've been doing this rotation for two decades on this land. I know what it needs. My family depends on this — four mouths, and a few of us pull income from outside work too, so I can't afford to gamble on the farm, but I also can't be wasteful with inputs I'm paying for myself.

**My thinking on wheat:** Winter wheat goes in around October 10th, as usual. I buy certified improved seed from the county seed station — I stopped using saved seed years ago after watching neighbors get better yields with certified varieties. I do rotary tillage after maize harvest to chop the stover and work it in. Fertilizer I apply mostly as base before sowing: diammonium phosphate for the phosphorus and potassium, then urea as topdress at jointing. Irrigation I plan three times — the pre-winter water in November to help establishment, then at jointing in late March, and again at heading. If it's a dry year I might squeeze in a fourth but three is my baseline. Two rounds of pesticide — one herbicide pass in November or early spring, and one fungicide plus aphid spray around heading time.

**My thinking on maize:** Summer maize I direct-seed right after wheat harvest in mid-June, no-till, to save time and moisture. I only use hybrid seed — that's been the only sensible choice for fifteen years. I apply compound fertilizer as base at sowing and top up with urea around the big-bell stage. With the well I can irrigate if we hit a dry stretch, but most years summer rains cover most of it — I budget two irrigations. One pesticide pass if I see fall armyworm pressure; otherwise maybe just a herbicide at early stage.
